content: A fitness trail, also known as a par course (derived from the French word parcours, meaning course), is a designated path or route that incorporates various obstacles or exercise stations along its length. These stations are specifically designed to facilitate physical activity and promote overall health and well-being. The concept of the fitness trail is rooted in the physical fitness training philosophy attributed to Georges Hébert. Fitness trails can be either natural or man-made and are commonly found in locations such as forests, transportation rights-of-way, parks, or urban environments. The equipment along these trails is designed to provide targeted forms of physiological exercise. This equipment may include natural features like climbable rocks, trees, or river embankments, as well as manufactured structures such as stepping posts, chin-up bars, and climbing bars, all of which are intended to offer physical challenges. The difficulty level of a fitness trail is influenced by factors such as the slope of the terrain, the type of trail surface (e.g., dirt, grass, gravel), the height of obstacles (e.g., walls), the length of certain challenges (e.g., crawl spaces), and other features. Urban fitness trails are typically designed to be flat, making them accessible to older adults and accommodating a variety of users, including cyclists, runners, skaters, and walkers. A modern evolution of the fitness trail is the outdoor gym, which features traditional gym equipment specifically designed for outdoor use. This concept is considered an extension of the par course. The original par course was invented in 1968 by Swiss architect Erwin Weckemann, with support from a Swiss insurance company. By 1972, hundreds of such courses had been constructed across Europe. In the United States, notable examples include the Parcour exercise trail established in 1976 at County Farm Park in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and the Bruce Jenner Trail created in 1977 in the Lake County Forest Preserve District in Illinois. In Hong Kong's New Territories, the Lion Rock Country Park, established in 1977, featured 15 exercise stations. Examples of fitness trails include the Chernikoff Fitness Trail in Prince George County Parks and Recreation, Maryland, USA; a maintained list of Parcours Fitness Trails in the Puget Sound area of Washington State, USA; and the Queens Park Fitness Trail in Invercargill, New Zealand. The fitness trail equipment industry offers standardized multi-station equipment packages for par courses. These packages are available from several manufacturers, including Columbia Cascade, Fit Trail, GameTime, Outdoor Fitness Equipment, and TriActive America.
